walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Members of a homologous series share:
options: The same molecular mass
The same functional group and general formula
The same boiling point
The same number of isomers

mcqs.q: What are the units of Kc for a reaction?
options: A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
Kc always has units of mol dm^-3.
Kc is always dimensionless.
They depend on Δn (the difference between moles of gaseous/aqueous products and reactants) — Kc can be dimensionless or have units like mol dm^-3.

mcqs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
options: Graphite conducts because it is a metal, while diamond is a non-metal.
Kc is always dimensionless.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond has all four outer electrons in localised covalent bonds.

mcqs.q: Does adding a catalyst change the value of Kc?
options: A catalyst increases Kc by favouring product formation.
No — a catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so Kc is unchanged.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stereoisomerism”?
options: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.
Shows movement of a pair of electrons during a reaction mechanism.
Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.
Same structural formula but different spatial arrangement; includes E/Z and optical isomers.

Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.

Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Structural isomerism”?
options: Shows movement of a pair of electrons during a reaction mechanism.

Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.
Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Functional group”?
options: An atom or group of atoms that determines the characteristic chemical behaviour of a molecule.
Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.
Same structural formula but different spatial arrangement; includes E/Z and optical isomers.
Family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by CH₂.
